summary.headline: Salzer Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38.4% YoY to Rs 579.77 crore, but EBITDA margin was 6.89% vs 8.73% a year ago; FY27 margin guided to about 8%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 579.77 crore in Q2 FY27, up 38.4% YoY and up from Rs 498.02 crore in Q1. EBITDA margin was 6.89% (vs 8.73% in Q2 FY26 and 6.29% in Q1), with H1 margin at 6.61% vs 9.91%. Profit after tax for Q2 was Rs 14.87 crore vs Rs 13.39 crore a year ago, while H1 PAT fell to Rs 23.2 crore from Rs 30.61 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze mainly to switchgear, where raw material price pass-through lags, and guided to gradual recovery in Q3 and Q4 with FY27 margin around 8% and FY28 at 9-10%.

segments.name: Industrial switchgear
segments.commentary: Contributed 56.39% of Q2 revenue (55.09% in H1), up 23.79% YoY; division EBITDA margin 8.26% in Q2. Bears the brunt of raw material pass-through lag. Utilisation about 80%.

segments.name: Wires and cables
segments.commentary: Contributed 36.18% of Q2 revenue (38.08% in H1), up 57.48% YoY per the call; EBITDA margin 5.08% in Q2. Largely run on cost-plus with customers, so margins stated as stable. Utilisation about 65%.

segments.name: Building products
segments.commentary: Contributed 7.43% of Q2 revenue (6.82% in H1), up 3.53% YoY in the quarter. Retail expanded beyond five southern states into Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

segments.name: KC Industries (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 17.95 crore (+20.4% YoY); EBITDA Rs 2.58 crore at 14.37% margin; PAT Rs 1.7 crore. H1 EBITDA Rs 4.55 crore at 13.82% margin; H1 PAT Rs 2.86 crore, broadly flat.

segments.name: Smart meters
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 2.87 crore; about Rs 3 crore in the quarter per Q&A. Management said execution remains challenging; about Rs 50 crore invested. Estimated drag of 0.7-1% on EBITDA/PAT; breakeven needs about Rs 25-30 crore quarterly turnover.

segments.name: Associate projects (Street light automation and EV charging)
segments.commentary: Rs 200 crore Bengaluru street light automation via SPV Filem (49% stake, equity-accounted), about Rs 2.2 crore/month for 84 months, now delayed to February 2027 from Q3 FY27. EV ultra-fast charging via associate: about 85 charges and about Rs 9 crore revenue this year; plan to double next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at about Rs 2,100 crore (about 30%+ YoY growth per analyst arithmetic).
FY27 EBITDA margin guided around 7.5-8% (around 8% per later remarks), with progressive normalisation from Q3 and Q4 subject to stable raw material prices.
FY28 EBITDA margin expected at about 9-10%, which management later referred to as close to its 10% target.

Saudi Arabia plant (cable ducts and terminal connectors first) delayed to April 2027 from Sept/Oct 2026; about Rs 15 crore investment over one year; first-year revenue not above Rs 20 crore, scaling to about Rs 100 crore in three years.
Net working capital days reduced to 135 from 153 (March 2026); management said a similar reduction would continue. Target to keep working capital within about 25% of revenue.
Medium-term export share target about 25% of revenue (21.3% in H1 FY27).
capex_capacity: Switchgear utilisation about 80%, judged sufficient for FY27 growth; balancing equipment capex planned for FY28 to add about 20-25% capacity, described as not capex-heavy.
Wires and cables utilisation about 65%; no major capacity investment expected in the near term.

FY27 capex expected to stay modest, apart from the Saudi Arabia project and expansion at the Ozoor facility; capital work in progress closing balance about Rs 11 crore, mainly buildings and switchgear equipment.
Smart meter facility fully integrated with 4 million units per annum capacity and a certified RF mesh platform; capex already spent.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for industrial switchgear remained healthy in Q2; pricing actions were taken over recent months, with realisation lagging order booking and execution.

Raw material costs (copper, aluminium, plastics, silver) rose about 40-50% per the CFO; management said copper and silver have stabilised and softened slightly, and the company is passing on the cost increases.
Wires and cables: about 70% of segment revenue is copper-linked (management estimate).
Data centres: company supplies magnet wire, cable harnesses and switchgear to OEMs making data-centre products, not directly to data centres.
Railways: cost-optimised versions helped win tenders; HVAC demand for the US improving after tariff moderation.

qa_highlights.question: Does H2 need above 8% EBITDA margin to reach the 7.5% full-year target, and what drives Q3-Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wires and cables margins are stable, the pressure sits in switchgear, and pricing actions taken in recent months will flow through in Q3 and Q4. It expects full-year EBITDA around 7.5-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No; the original guidance of about Rs 2,100 crore for FY27 is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material hedging being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging has been explored but not implemented for any commodity so far.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi Arabia plant's investment, timing and revenue ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 15 crore over one year; operations from April 2027; first-year revenue not above Rs 20 crore, reaching about Rs 100 crore in three years; breakeven expected in year two.

qa_highlights.question: What is smart meter breakeven and margin drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven needs about Rs 25-30 crore quarterly turnover at the standalone level; drag on EBITDA/PAT is estimated at 0.7-1%. About Rs 50 crore invested so far; orders are being pursued via EPC contractors.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost and leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost was about 2.3-2.4% of sales, down from about 3%, though absolute finance cost rose about Rs 2 crore YoY. Management said debt-to-equity of 0.92 is expected to ease as volumes and margins recover; no immediate capital raise, though options are being explored.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on pass-through of price hikes and on copper/silver prices staying stable; the company said it has not hedged commodities.

Saudi Arabia plant and the Bengaluru street light project have both slipped (to April 2027 and February 2027 respectively); further delay risk tied to Middle East conditions and project documentation.
Leverage rising: debt-to-equity cited at 0.92, the highest in four years, with receivables and working capital rising.
Smart meter order intake remains weak; no firm order pipeline or revenue projection was given.
Export share fell to 21.3% in H1 FY27 from about 24% last year, against a 25% medium-term target.
Management did not disclose the split of copper, silver and aluminium in raw materials for switchgear, which is needed to model input-cost sensitivity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium- to long-term electrical infrastructure demand but cautious on near-term margins; management repeatedly said the margin recovery will be progressive and depend on commodity prices and customer acceptance of price revisions. Several project timelines (Saudi Arabia, Filem street lights, smart meters) were pushed out, and answers on smart meters and switchgear order books were vague.
key_quotes: Subject to Romitl prices remaining stable, we expect margins to normalize progressively from the third and the fourth quarter of this financial year.

In our wiring cable division, which is largely run on cost plus basis with customers, margins have remained relatively stable while the pressure is concentrated in our switch gear business where price variation costs exist, but pass-through is not immediate.
We have explored the possibility of doing some aging, but we have so far refined aging any projects, any commodity as of now.
Smart meter revenue for H1 FY 27 was at 2.87 crores as the execution remains challenging.
